Q1: Which mechanism should keep the leftover gaps tracked?
Choices:
A. Option A: for a partial delivery, the PR body uses `Refs <issue>` instead of `Closes`. After the merge, the pipeline posts a comment on the issue listing the remaining items and sends the issue back into clarify for the rest. The `activation_fix_merge` skip stays as it is. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Option B: keep `Closes`. Before the PR is opened or merged, file a new issue for the remaining items, reusing the original `<!-- ai:activation-fix:v1 source=<key> -->` so de-duplication still works.
C. Both: keep the issue open (A), and also file a follow-up issue when the original is an activation-fix issue.
Q2: Which issues does the partial-delivery handling cover?
Choices:
A. Every pipeline-implemented standalone issue whose delivery is deliberately partial. The #4639 case is the regression test. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Only activation-fix issues (first body line `<!-- ai:activation-fix:v1 source=... -->`).
**Note:** Q1:B reuses the activation-fix source marker, so it only fits Q2:B. Choosing Q1:B with Q2:A would need a separate follow-up format for ordinary issues.
Q3: What counts as proof that a delivery is deliberately partial? Closing must stay the default when this signal is missing.
Choices:
A. A new structured block in the plan, such as `Deferred scope:` with one bullet per remaining item. The plan prompt requires it whenever an answer or auto-decision limits scope, and implement reads it from the approved plan comment. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Treat the delivery as partial whenever the approved plan's `Scope-mode:` is `Reduction`, and take the remaining items from the `Scope-mode justification:` text.
C. Parse the clarify answers and auto-decision (`AD-<n>`) entries for scope-limiting picks, such as "Phase 1 only".
Q4: Should the related gap (a sweep that finds open, unlabelled, never-clarified issues from trusted authors and posts `/reclarify` once) be built here?
Choices:
A. Split it into a separate issue, and keep this issue to partial-delivery tracking only. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Include it in this issue, in the poller's standalone stall-recovery sweep, behind a default-on kill switch.
